# Dozable

> Dozable runs teams of AI coding agents on your Mac. Each agent runs where you choose: in its own micro VM or held to its folder on your Mac, where your keys never go inside, or as you. Free and open source.

The user manual for Dozable, which runs teams of AI coding agents on your Mac: install, set up, make workspaces, and run each agent in its own micro VM or held to its folder, with the doz command or its dashboard.

Pages have Markdown twins: add `.md` to a page URL (`/docs/` is `/docs/index.md`; the home page is `/index.html.md`).

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://dozable.com/docs/getting-started.md): Dozable runs teams of AI coding agents on your Mac.
- [Installing, upgrading and uninstalling](https://dozable.com/docs/install-upgrade-uninstall.md): doz is one command-line program. It comes with everything it needs inside it: the small Linux programs each sandbox uses, the Linux kernel sandboxes boot (so the first start downloads no kernel), the web dashboard, and the permission macOS requires to run virtual machines.
- [Setting up this Mac](https://dozable.com/docs/setting-up.md): Setup — onboarding — is what you do once after installing: it checks your Mac, prepares the base image every tool is added to, adds the keys your tools use, chooses and confirms what sandboxes may use as you (Access: GitHub, your SSH agent), explains folder rules and lets you choose what they do, writes your settings, and makes your first sandbox.
- [Projects](https://dozable.com/docs/projects.md): A project is a folder with a doz_project.yaml file in it.
- [Sandboxes and their lifecycle](https://dozable.com/docs/sandboxes-and-lifecycle.md): A sandbox is one Linux virtual machine with its own disks.
- [The dashboard (`doz ui`)](https://dozable.com/docs/the-dashboard.md): doz ui is Dozable in your browser: every sandbox with a live terminal, its restore points and permissions, your images, accounts, disk use and settings.
- [Terminals and sessions](https://dozable.com/docs/terminals-and-sessions.md): A session is a terminal program running inside a sandbox: a shell, claude, pi, a dev server.
- [Images and bases](https://dozable.com/docs/images-and-bases.md): Every sandbox starts from a baked image: a disk with a Linux system, a developer toolkit and, usually, the agent a recipe installs.
- [Agents and accounts](https://dozable.com/docs/agents-and-accounts.md): Dozable runs three AI coding agents out of the box — Claude Code, pi and OpenAI's Codex — and gives each one the account it should use, without the secret ever entering the sandbox.
- [What the agent can do: permissions and the network](https://dozable.com/docs/permissions-and-network.md): A sandbox has no network card. Its only way out is a proxy in Dozable's host, on your Mac, which checks every connection against the sandbox's permissions — a short list of plain-language switches — and logs it.
- [Signing in from a sandbox](https://dozable.com/docs/signing-in-from-a-sandbox.md): Many command-line tools sign you in through a web browser: they open a sign-in page, you sign in, and the provider sends your browser back to the tool on http://localhost:PORT.
- [Restore points, duplicates and saved disks](https://dozable.com/docs/restore-points-duplicates-templates.md): Three ways to copy a sandbox's disk, each instant (they're APFS clones, sharing space until something changes).
- [Resources and disk space](https://dozable.com/docs/resources-and-disk-space.md): Dozable keeps everything in one folder, the store.
- [Letting another agent drive Dozable](https://dozable.com/docs/letting-another-agent-drive.md): So far you have run doz. But the agent you already use on your Mac — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor — can run it too.
- [Settings reference](https://dozable.com/docs/settings-reference.md): This Mac's settings are in one file, ~/.config/doz/doz.toml (under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME when that is set).
- [Security model](https://dozable.com/docs/security-model.md): Dozable's job is to let an AI agent work freely — install things, run code, make a mess — without putting your Mac, your credentials or your data at risk.
- [Troubleshooting and FAQ](https://dozable.com/docs/troubleshooting-and-faq.md): doz doctor first; then find your error below by its words.
- [GitHub as you](https://dozable.com/docs/github.md): An agent on your Mac uses git and gh as you: it clones your private repositories, opens pull requests, comments on issues.
- [Managed tools](https://dozable.com/docs/the-tools-layer.md): Some settings need a tool inside the sandbox to be useful: "GitHub as you" is best with gh, SSH agent forwarding needs an ssh client and GitHub's host keys, tmux sessions need tmux.
- [Folder rules: `.dozignore` and `.dozreadonly`](https://dozable.com/docs/workspace-rules.md): A sandbox's /workspace is your Mac folder, live. Often you want the agent to see most of it but not everything: not secrets.env, not your doz_project.yaml, not a folder of build output it would only wade through.
- [The folder view (`dozview`)](https://dozable.com/docs/the-workspace-view.md): /workspace inside a sandbox is not your shared folder itself: it is a live view of it, served by a small Dozable program, dozview.
- [Prompts for your agent](https://dozable.com/docs/prompts-for-your-agent.md): Your Mac's own coding agent — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor — can install Dozable, set it up and run sandboxes for you.
- [Sound](https://dozable.com/docs/sound.md): A sandbox can have sound: programs in it play through your Mac's speakers and, if you want, record from its microphone.
- [Codex](https://dozable.com/docs/codex.md): OpenAI's Codex runs in a Dozable sandbox the way Claude Code does: ready to work, without approval prompts (the Sandbox and its network are the boundary), told where it runs, and with its credential kept on your Mac — it never enters the sandbox.
- [The dashboard on your other computers, tablets and phones (`doz ui --lan`)](https://dozable.com/docs/doz-serve.md): doz ui is one dashboard. Without its LAN option it listens on 127.0.0.1 and nothing but this Mac can reach it.
- [Trying agents, and what Dozable supports](https://dozable.com/docs/try-and-search.md): doz try takes you from nothing to talking to an agent in one command.
- [More agents: Antigravity CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot CLI, Qwen Code, Goose, Kilo Code CLI, Mistral Vibe, Factory Droid, Dirac, Kimi Code, Cline CLI, OpenHands CLI, Letta Code, Docker Agent, Nanocoder, mini-swe-agent, Open Interpreter, Crush, MiMo Code, CodeWhale, Maki, oh-my-pi, Tau, Gemini CLI](https://dozable.com/docs/more-agents.md): Beside Claude Code, pi and Codex, Dozable runs agents from other makers.
- [Other AI tools](https://dozable.com/docs/ai-tools.md): Beside the coding agents, Dozable runs AI tools that are not coding agents: command-line tools that answer a prompt, prompt toolkits, agent frameworks.
- [Web ports: opening a sandbox's web page on your Mac](https://dozable.com/docs/web-ports.md): Some tools serve a web page from inside the sandbox: a chat playground, a workflow editor, the dev server of the app you are building.
- [Your own recipes, and community catalogues](https://dozable.com/docs/your-own-recipes.md): Every tool Dozable runs comes from a recipe: a YAML file that says how the tool is installed, how it runs, which key it uses and what it may reach.
- [Your dotfiles](https://dozable.com/docs/dotfiles.md): A new sandbox has a stock shell: no aliases, no prompt of yours, no editor settings.
- [Claude Code with other models — a gateway, or a model server on your Mac](https://dozable.com/docs/claude-code-other-models.md): Claude Code talks to Anthropic by default: this Mac's Claude login, a setup token or an Anthropic API key, exactly as in Agents and accounts.
- [Bundling doz in an app](https://dozable.com/docs/bundling-doz-in-an-app.md): If you want Dozable on your Mac, install the doz command with Homebrew (Installing, upgrading and uninstalling).
- [Sessions on this Mac](https://dozable.com/docs/sessions-on-this-mac.md): Every other page of this manual is about sandboxes: a program in its own small Linux machine, with a network that reaches only what you allow and none of your keys.
- [The menu bar app](https://dozable.com/docs/the-menu-bar-app.md): Dozable's daemon is the background process that runs your sandboxes.
- [Chat](https://dozable.com/docs/chat.md): Chat is a set of rooms on your Mac where you and your agents talk: you in the dashboard or a terminal, each agent with its own token.
- [Workspaces](https://dozable.com/docs/workspaces.md): A workspace is an environment set up for getting work done: its agents, its rooms, the brief that says what the work is for, and any folders it works on (usually projects).
- [Agents / Bots](https://dozable.com/docs/agents-and-bots.md): An Agent / Bot is a lasting identity in chat: a participant with a name that stays, its agent program (Claude Code, Codex, …), its model and account, where it runs, how the chat server reaches it, and a token of its own.
- [Space files](https://dozable.com/docs/space-files.md): A space file describes a workspace in one YAML file, NAME.space.yaml, kept in git beside the work: its agents, its rooms, the brief, any folders and sandboxes.
- [History and retention](https://dozable.com/docs/history-and-retention.md): Dozable keeps a history of what happened on this Mac — every action on a sandbox, sessions, the daemon's runs and its events, each sandbox's connections and network by minute, CPU, memory and disk samples, the use of your keys (by name), workspace and permission logs, runs and their frames, and the times of chat messages and the outcomes of Asks — and answers it as one timeline: doz timeline.
- [Runs, the journal and lessons](https://dozable.com/docs/runs-the-journal-and-lessons.md): A run is one unit of work in a workspace, from its start to its finish: a goal, the agents working on it, the conversation in its room, and a journal that records what was done.
- [Bring your own process: a worked example](https://dozable.com/docs/bring-your-own-process.md): Dozable does not come with a process. It gives you the parts — a workspace with a brief, a room, agents, units of work (runs) and a journal for each, lessons that carry into the next — and you decide how they are used.
- [Tokens and identity](https://dozable.com/docs/tokens-and-identity.md): In chat, every agent is someone: a participant with a name, and a token that proves it.
- [Feeds and notices](https://dozable.com/docs/feeds-and-notices.md): A room holds people and agents. Some facts come from neither: a unit of work's outcome in its journal, this Mac's Claude login expiring, the network refusing a host again and again, an agent that crashed, the disk running low.
- [The manual — contents](https://dozable.com/docs/index.md): every chapter in reading order.

## Blog

- [Blog index](https://dozable.com/blog/index.md): news, early access, tips and tricks.
- [Dozable 0.51 - chat rooms, and fenced sessions on your Mac](https://dozable.com/blog/doz-v0.51.md): Dozable 0.51 adds chat rooms for you and your agents, fences sessions on your Mac by default, keeps the daemon running with a menu bar app, and can publish the dashboard on your tailnet.
- [Working together with Grok Bot in a Claude Code session, enabled by Dozable](https://dozable.com/blog/grok-bot-claude-dozable.md): Claude Code superpowers granted to your Grok Bots.
- [Dozable 0.37 - sessions on this Mac](https://dozable.com/blog/doz-v0.37.md): Dozable 0.37 holds sessions on this Mac for work a Linux sandbox cannot do, and adds Claude Code with local models, your own recipes, and dotfiles in every sandbox.
- [Dozer Sandbox is now Dozable](https://dozable.com/blog/dozable.md): Dozer Sandbox has a new name, Dozable, in 0.36.1; the doz command, your sandboxes, your settings and how you upgrade all stay as they are.
- [Dozable 0.35 - doz try, and keys from any provider](https://dozable.com/blog/doz-v0.35.md): Dozable 0.35 adds doz try for any of 42 coding agents and AI tools, keys from any major provider or gateway, a choice of model, and OpenCode 2.
- [doz try - any of 42 AI tools in one command](https://dozable.com/blog/doz-try.md): doz try puts you in a throwaway sandbox with a coding agent or AI tool, its own empty folder, a network that reaches only its model and your key kept on your Mac.
- [OpenCode 2 is in Dozable](https://dozable.com/blog/opencode-2.md): OpenCode 2, a rebuild of the open-source coding agent around one shared background service, now runs in Dozable beside OpenCode 1, on your own key or OpenCode Zen's free models.
- [Grok Build now tells Dozable what it's doing](https://dozable.com/blog/grok-build-status.md): Grok Build 1.0.52 reports when it's working, waiting for you or done, and Dozable 0.35 shows it in the dashboard, as it does for Claude Code and pi.
- [Introducing Dozable](https://dozable.com/blog/introducing-dozable.md): Fast, resumable, secure Linux sandboxes for AI coding agents on your Mac — free and open source. Here's what it is, why it exists, and how to try it in a minute.
- [Dozable 0.33 - see what your agent is doing](https://dozable.com/blog/dozable-0-33.md): Dozable 0.33 shows what each agent is doing at a glance, upgrades with one command, runs the dashboard in the background, and ends setup with an optional sign-up.
